Exercise 10.1-3 (two stacks in one array): Stack A grows from 1 upward; stack B grows from n downward. Overflow only when A.top
+ 1 > B.top. Exercise 10.1-4 (queue trace): ENQUEUE(4), ENQUEUE(1), ENQUEUE(3), DEQUEUE, ENQUEUE(8), DEQUEUE on Q[1:6].

h=1,t=1→h=1,t=2[4]→h=1,t=3[4,1]→h=1,t=4[4,1,3]→DEQ returns 4,h=2→h=2,t=5[1,3,8]→DEQ returns 1,h=3. Final h=3,t=5, Q=
[3,8,,,_]. Exercise 10.1-5: Full/empty checks in ENQUEUE/DEQUEUE: ENQUEUE: if Q.head==Q.tail+1 or (Q.head==1 and Q.tail==Q.size):
overflow. DEQUEUE: if Q.head==Q.tail: underflow.

Exercise 10.1-6 (deque via array): maintain 4 operations: PUSH-FRONT, POP-FRONT, PUSH-BACK, POP-BACK. Use circular
array with head and tail mod n. Exercise 10.1-7 (queue via two stacks): ENQUEUE: push to stack1. DEQUEUE: if stack2 empty, pop all from stack1 → push to
stack2; then pop from stack2.

Amortized O(1), worst-case O(n) per DEQUEUE. Exercise 10.1-8 (stack via two queues): PUSH: enqueue to queue1. POP: move all but last from queue1 to queue2, dequeue last
from queue1, swap queues. O(n) per POP. Exercise 10.2-1: Singly linked INSERT = O(1) (prepend at head).

DELETE = Θ(n) (must find predecessor). Exercise 10.2-2 (stack via singly linked list): PUSH = LIST-PREPEND. POP = remove head. Only L.head needed. Exercise 10.2-3 (queue via singly linked list): ENQUEUE at tail O(1) with tail pointer. DEQUEUE at head O(1). Need L.head and
L.tail.

Exercise 10.2-4: UNION in O(1): set tail of L1’s last element (via tail pointer) to point to head of L2. Exercise 10.2-5 (reverse singly linked): prev=NIL, curr=head. While curr≠NIL: next=curr.next; curr.next=prev; prev=curr; curr=next. Return prev. Θ(n), O(1) extra space.

Exercise 10.2-6 (XOR doubly linked): x.np = x.next XOR x.prev. To traverse forward from head (prev=NIL=0): next = prev XOR
curr.np. To reverse: swap direction pointers. Problem 10-2 (mergeable heaps): (a) Sorted lists: INSERT O(n), UNION O(n), MIN O(1), EXTRACT-MIN O(1).

(b) Unsorted:
INSERT O(1), MIN Θ(n), EXTRACT-MIN Θ(n), UNION O(1). (c) Unsorted disjoint: UNION O(1) with tail pointer. Problem 10-3 (COMPACT-LIST-SEARCH): Expected O(√n) with random skips. Requires distinct keys. O(t + n/(t+1)) expected with t
random skips. Optimize t=√n.

Example: Full Deque via Array

Maintain Q[1:n], with head and tail. PUSH-FRONT: head = (head-2 mod n)+1; Q[head]=x. POP-FRONT: x=Q[head]; head=(head mod
n)+1. PUSH-BACK: Q[tail]=x; tail=(tail mod n)+1. POP-BACK: tail=(tail-2 mod n)+1; return Q[tail]. All O(1).
Example: XOR Linked List in Detail

List: head→[5]↔[2]↔[7]↔[9]→NIL (values 5,2,7,9). Each node stores np = next XOR prev. Starting from head (prev=NIL=0): - curr.np = 0
XOR next = next → to traverse, next = prev XOR curr.np - Forward from head: prev=0, curr=head=5. np[5]=0 XOR addr[2] = addr[2].

Next
= 0 XOR addr[2] = addr[2] (node 2). Now prev=addr[5], curr=addr[2]. np[2]=addr[5] XOR addr[7]. Next = addr[5] XOR (addr[5] XOR
addr[7]) = addr[7]. Continue: next = addr[2] XOR (addr[2] XOR addr[9]) = addr[9]. Next = addr[7] XOR (addr[7] XOR 0) = 0 (NIL). Done. -
